definitions.explanation: An organism, typically bacteria or fungi, that breaks down dead organic matter and returns nutrients to the ecosystem.

examples.japanese: キノコは{分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: Mushrooms are one type of decomposer.

examples.japanese: {分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}は{生態系|せいたいけい}で{重要|じゅうよう}な{役割|やくわり}を{果|は}たす。
examples.english: Decomposers play an important role in ecosystems.

examples.japanese: {分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}がいなければ、{落|お}ち{葉|ば}や{動物|どうぶつ}の{死骸|しがい}が{分解|ぶんかい}されない。
examples.english: Without decomposers, fallen leaves and animal carcasses would not be broken down.

notes:
{分解者|ぶんかいしゃ} is a biology term composed of {分解|ぶんかい} (decomposition) + {者|しゃ} (one who does). It refers to organisms that break down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

ECOSYSTEM ROLES (commonly taught as a set):
- {生産者|せいさんしゃ}: producer (plants — make food via photosynthesis)
- {消費者|しょうひしゃ}: consumer (animals — eat other organisms)
- {分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}: decomposer (break down dead matter)

EXAMPLES OF DECOMPOSERS:
- {細菌|さいきん}: bacteria
- {菌類|きんるい}: fungi (including mushrooms and mold)
- ミミズ: earthworms

USAGE:
This term appears frequently in {理科|りか} (science) classes and {生態系|せいたいけい} (ecosystem) discussions. The three-role classification is a standard part of Japanese science education.
